quote: We built machines to save time, then spent all our time keeping up with them.
We keep automating the future, but forget to ask who it's actually for.
We mistake speed for progress, then wonder why we never arrive anywhere.
We taught machines to learn, then forgot to keep learning ourselves.
We're not adapting to the future, we're just outsourcing it.
The smarter our tools become, the less we question where they're leading us.
Automation doesn't remove the hard choices, it just hides them behind a smoother interface.
Every efficiency we gain quietly asks us what we were saving the time for.
Progress keeps arriving faster than we can decide what to do with it.
We automate the questions we're too busy to actually answer.
Strategy without decisiveness is just an expensive way of staying still.
Indecision is the only strategy guaranteed to fail.
Clarity beats consensus; a decision made today outperforms a perfect one made too late.
